name: Bullpen — Part 4 (planned)
description: Prediction, not yet built: placing a paper trade becomes a durable order saga that drives each order to a fill, a cancel or a retry. Orders and the ledger stay together: every step is one transaction in the trading schema, owned by the Trading App. Market data, the Bullpen Database and the daily cron carry forward from Part 3.

nodes.name: Reader
nodes.description: A blog reader exploring Bullpen's architecture timeline on the landing site.

nodes.name: Player
nodes.description: A registered player who places paper trade orders.

nodes.name: Bullpen Landing
nodes.description: The public landing site with the architecture timeline explorer.

nodes.name: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.description: The trading app where players view prices and submit paper trade orders. It owns orders, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view in the trading schema.

nodes.name: Order Saga
nodes.description: Durable workflow driving each order to a fill, a cancel or a retry. Each step is one transaction in the trading schema, so the order and the ledger change together; compensation covers a step that fails.

nodes.name: Market Data Service
nodes.description: The single owner of market data: both providers (stocks end of day, crypto) and both call budgets. It serves the public price route and the daily ingest. It is a boundary inside one release, not an independently deployed microservice.

nodes.name: CoinGecko
nodes.description: CoinGecko's free Demo API (api.coingecko.com), called for BTC-USD price snapshots. Chosen after a Coinbase-based design was ruled out by Coinbase's Terms of Use, which forbid public display of their data (see issue #6, ADR-0005, docs/data-sources.md).

nodes.name: Alpha Vantage
nodes.description: External market-data API for U.S. stock prices: end of day, one request per symbol, fetched once a day by the Market Data service within a daily call budget (ADR-0008).

relationships.description: Reader browses the public landing site.
Trading app starts an order saga for each accepted order.
Trading app requests a live price for a symbol: GET /api/price/<symbol>, rewritten to the Market Data service.
The Market Data service fetches a crypto price from CoinGecko, after reserving a call against its budget.
The Market Data service fetches each stock's end-of-day price once a day, after reserving a call against the daily budget.
